Arkham Falls in the New Batman: Knightfall Preview

by Sharna Jahangir September 7, 2026
by Sharna Jahangir September 7, 2026 0 comment
236
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:16
Instaread

Gotham City has descended into absolute chaos, and the Dark Knight is facing his ultimate breaking point. Dark Knight News is thrilled to announce that the highly anticipated animated feature, Batman: Knightfall Part 1: Knightfall, is finally making its debut!

After the catastrophic destruction of Arkham Asylum, the city unleashes. Every dangerous, maniacal, and psychotic inmate has flooded the streets of Gotham, creating a criminal tide that threatens to drown the city forever. In this epic animated adaptation of the legendary DC comics storyline, Batman races against time to round up his greatest foes; including our faves: the Joker, Scarecrow, and Killer Croc.

But this is just the beginning. As the Bat pushes to his absolute physical and mental limits, a new, hulking threat emerges from the shadows. The man called Bane has arrived, and he intends to break the Bat once and for all.

Watch the full movie preview now: 

You can experience the complete, stunningly animated, action-packed story right now, as the film is available TODAY on Digital HD.

For those who prefer to own the physical media, mark your calendars. Batman: Knightfall Part 1: Knightfall will be released in stunning 4K UHD, Blu-ray, and DVD on September 8th. This release promises to include exclusive behind-the-scenes features, commentary, and bonus content, making it an absolute must-have for any collector.

Voices behind the film

The cast delivers a powerhouse performance, with each actor bringing their distinct talents to these iconic characters. Anson Mount, celebrated for his role as Captain Pike in Star Trek: Strange New Worlds, takes on the dual role of Bruce Wayne and Batman, and critics have praised his performance for capturing the character’s profound exhaustion and mental strain . He intentionally steps away from a rough, throaty growl, instead allowing a ragged weariness to bleed into his delivery, perfectly visualizing a hero pushed to his breaking point .

As the formidable Bane, Michael Mando (known for Better Call Saul and Scorpion in the blockbuster Spider-Man: Brand New Day) delivers a performance so impressive that the supervising producer didn’t change a single line of his dialogue . Mando took a deeply analytical approach. He learns the entire script to craft a unique voice that bends words the way Bane bends wills, all grounded in the character’s underlying pain.

Finally, Pablo Schreiber (Halo) steps into the role of Jean-Paul Valley/Azrael, a character who many reviewers feel steals the show as his arc becomes increasingly central to the saga . Together, these talented actors bring a fresh intensity to the classic storyline, grounding the psychological action in truly compelling performances.

What we’re excited for!

This film is a masterclass in the classic Batman formula. Intense action, deep psychological stakes, and a villain so formidable that he redefines the meaning of fear. The animation looks crisp. The voice cast is top-tier, and the story pulls zero punches. A perfect recipe capturing the exhaustion and desperation of a hero pushed beyond his limits.

Don’t miss out on the comic event of the autumn season. Whether you are a lifelong fan of the classic Knightfall arc or a newcomer to the animated DC Universe, this is the definitive way to see the Bat-Breaking saga unfold.
